items.definition: The three functional forces: Vata (movement), Pitta (transformation), Kapha (structure and cohesion).
The seven tissues: Rasa, Rakta, Mamsa, Meda, Asthi, Majja, Shukra.
Wastes: Purisha (stool), Mutra (urine), Sveda (sweat).
Digestive and metabolic fire: one Jatharagni, five Bhutagnis, seven Dhatvagnis.
Undigested, sticky material from weak agni; the root of many diseases.
Body channels that carry dosha, dhatu and mala; blocked or vitiated srotas cause disease.
The essence of all tissues; the basis of immunity and strength.
A person's constitution, fixed at conception by the dominant doshas.
Pathogenesis: how vitiated doshas travel and lodge to cause disease.
Sushruta's six stages of disease: Sanchaya, Prakopa, Prasara, Sthana Samshraya, Vyakti, Bheda.
Five diagnostic tools: Nidana (cause), Purvarupa (prodrome), Rupa (signs), Upashaya (therapeutic test), Samprapti.
How a drug acts: taste, qualities, potency (hot or cold), post-digestive effect and special action.
Five cleansing procedures: Vamana, Virechana, Basti (two kinds: Niruha and Anuvasana) and Nasya; Sushruta adds Raktamokshana.
The vehicle taken with a medicine (water, honey, ghee, milk) that guides and boosts its action.
Diet and conduct that support treatment; Apathya is what harms it.
The dosha of movement (air and space): breathing, circulation, nerve impulses, elimination. Dry, light, cold, rough, mobile.
The dosha of transformation (fire and water): digestion, metabolism, body heat, vision, intellect. Hot, sharp, light, oily.
The dosha of structure and cohesion (water and earth): lubrication, stability, immunity. Heavy, cold, oily, slow, stable.
Cleansing therapy that removes vitiated doshas from the body, chiefly by Panchakarma.
Palliative therapy that calms doshas inside the body with medicines, diet and lifestyle, without expelling them.
Rejuvenation therapy that promotes long life, immunity, memory and tissue quality.
Therapy for sexual health, fertility and vigour.
The daily routine: waking before dawn, cleansing, oil massage, exercise, bathing and regular meals.
Seasonal routine: changing diet and conduct with each of the six seasons.
Therapeutic emesis, the main Panchakarma for Kapha disorders.
Therapeutic purgation, the main Panchakarma for Pitta disorders.
Medicated enema, the main Panchakarma for Vata disorders; Charaka calls it half of all treatment.
Medicine given through the nose, for disorders of the head and neck.
Bloodletting (by leech, needle or cupping) for blood-borne disorders; Sushruta counts it as a fifth cleansing therapy.
Oil massage of the whole body, part of the daily routine and of pre-Panchakarma preparation.
Sweating therapy (fomentation, steam) to loosen doshas and relieve stiffness and pain.
A steady stream of warm oil, milk or buttermilk poured on the forehead for sleep, stress and headache.
Lightening therapy: fasting, light diet, exercise and drying measures.
Nourishing therapy that builds tissues and strength.
Mind-control therapy: counselling and restraint of the mind from harmful objects; Ayurveda's psychotherapy.
A decoction: coarse herb powder boiled in water and reduced, usually to a quarter.
A fine powder of dried herbs.
A tablet or pill (also called Gutika).
Medicated ghee, made by cooking ghee with herbal paste and liquid.
Medicated oil, made the same way as Ghrita but with oil (usually sesame).
Self-fermented liquid medicines: Asava from raw juices, Arishta from decoctions. They contain a little natural alcohol.
A medicated jam or confection (Leha), such as Chyavanaprasha.
Tablets made with purified Guggulu resin as the base, such as Yogaraja Guggulu.
A calcined metal or mineral ash prepared by repeated purification and heating; used in tiny doses in Rasa Shastra.
The branch of Ayurveda that prepares medicines from metals and minerals (mercury, sulphur, iron, gold and others).
The purification of a raw herb, mineral or metal before it can be used as medicine.
A therapeutic test: diagnosis from what relieves or aggravates the condition.
Early warning signs (prodrome) of a disease.
The fully developed signs and symptoms of a disease.
The tissue or waste that the vitiated dosha damages.
Channel disorder: excess flow, obstruction, swelling (granthi) or flow in the wrong path.
Prognosis: curable (easily or with effort), controllable (yapya) or incurable.
The eight branches: internal medicine, surgery, ENT and eye, paediatrics, psychiatry and spirits, toxicology, rejuvenation and sexual health.
The doctrine that health is the balance of Vata, Pitta and Kapha, and disease their imbalance.
The five great elements (space, air, fire, water, earth) of which all matter, body and medicine are made.
